experiment: surface-parcellation transfer with a random control
finding: On a single surface parcellation the block-weighting idea barely helps (flat 0.343 -> best 0.349) and the structured Yeo partition is indistinguishable from a RANDOM partition of the same sizes (0.3485 vs 0.3461). So the earlier +0.012 from equal 20-blocks was an averaging effect, not network structure.
implication: The large gain in the ICA case (+0.024 from sqrt weighting, +0.033 from partial correlation) comes from mixing genuinely DIFFERENT representations (full vs partial correlation), not from partitioning one representation into blocks.
honest_caveat: This is the strongest evidence so far that our method's advantage is representation-specific rather than a general-purpose trick, which weakens any claim that it would beat the literature on their own Schaefer pipeline.
